# Was Boeing hacked by the INC Ransom group?

**Not established.** Not established. INC Ransom claims it took 3.6 million files from a Boeing helicopter support unit. Boeing has said nothing, no filing exists, and no one independent has verified the claim.

Incident: Boeing ransomware claim by INC Ransom, Nov 20, 2026. Also reported as the Boeing leak-site claim and the Boeing helicopter unit claim. First published Nov 20, 2026; last updated Nov 20, 2026, 7:49 PM ET.

## The latest

Nov 20, 2026, 7:49 PM ET: **INC Ransom claims a Boeing helicopter support unit breach on Nov 20; Boeing has said nothing and no one has verified it.** First draft. 5 sources (2 Tier 1: Boeing newsroom and SEC filings, checked with no statement), 9 claims (3 Confirmed, 4 Reported, 1 Unverified, 1 Not established), 3 questions. ## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Local. The group claims 3.6 million files from one Boeing-linked support unit. None of it is verified, and Boeing has not said whether anything was taken.
- Who is affected: No one is confirmed to be affected. If the claim is true, it could involve staff, vendors and customers of one military helicopter support unit.

### Known so far

- INC Ransom listed Boeing on its leak site on Nov 20. This confirms the post exists, not that data was taken.
- Boeing has made no public statement about the claim as of Nov 20.
- Boeing has filed no cybersecurity 8-K as of Nov 20.

### Not known yet

- Whether any intrusion happened, and at which Boeing or joint-venture system.
- Whether the files and screenshots are real.
- Whether the unit is part of Boeing's own network.
- Whether Boeing will make a statement or file with the SEC.
- Whether the group will publish more data.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of 8 PM ET on Nov 20, 2026.

- A Boeing statement about the claim (the newsroom's latest release is a Nov 15 aircraft order).

- Independent verification of the screenshots or the file counts.
- A government statement about the claim.
- The leak site itself. We did not visit it; the claim is cited through a tracker and press.
